horizontal._comment: The dispatch webhook (app/server/routes/webhooks.py). horizontal.name: session-logs-original
horizontal._comment: RA-7407: the ORIGINAL build-log SSE route (sessions.py:104 stream_session_logs), distinct from the two entries above, which cover the RA-6504 hardened stream and its RA-6788 short alias. It was one of eight proxy-reachable routes with no smoke coverage. Status derived from a live call against a running server, not guessed: authenticated + absent sid returns 404 {"detail":"Session not found"} at sessions.py:119, raised BEFORE the StreamingResponse generator is constructed, so nothing streams and there is no side effect. auth:true is load-bearing — the same call unauthenticated returns 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} from require_auth, so an auth:false probe here would assert only the dashboard session gate and would stay green with the backend route deleted. The sid cannot collide with a real session: ids are uuid4().hex[:12] (session_model.py:42), and this one is 22 chars containing non-hex letters. NO QUERY STRING, deliberately: both siblings use ?after=0, so this is the only probe exercising the `$` branch of SSE_PATH_RE in the proxy (dashboard/app/api/pi-ceo/[...path]/route.ts:18); proxySse passes res.status through verbatim, so the 404 survives. DO NOT DROP body_contains — it is what makes this probe non-vacuous, and the status alone is not. Measured, not argued: with the backend route renamed away and the server restarted, this probe still returned 404 (FastAPI's own unknown-path 404) and the status assertion stayed GREEN; only body_contains caught it, because the body became {"detail":"Not Found"}. A status-only 404 probe here would be exactly the check-that-cannot-fail this entry exists to avoid. Verified end-to-end before landing, per the PR #650 caution recorded in the proxy allowlist: run against a local dashboard proxying a local backend, this probe returned 404 with the expected body in 14-18 ms, and four checksum-verified sabotages each made it fail — wrong expected_status, an unreachable body string, auth flipped to false (401 at the proxy, the webhook-dispatch-nosig failure mode), and the backend route deleted. The other seven undeclared reachable routes (POST build, scan, goal-projects, goal-ticket, goal-ticket/analyze, sessions/kill, sessions/resume) are deliberately NOT declared: their only safe probe is an auth:false 401 that proves nothing, and their strong probe runs a real build, scan, Linear ticket or session kill against production. Seven weak entries would raise the coverage count by seven while covering nothing, and RA-7402's ratchet would then lock them in permanently.

This probe therefore proves the dashboard's session gate refuses anonymous access to this path. It does NOT prove the backend route exists, nor that the route's own X-Pi-CEO-Secret check works — deleting the route file would leave this probe green. The same holds for every other auth:false probe under this prefix. It is NOT a property of the '-nosig' name, which refers to a missing webhook SIGNATURE: the auth:true members of that family (slack-margot-bridge-nosig, webhook-dispatch-nosig) pass the session gate and do reach the backend. horizontal.name: proxy-goal-projects
horizontal._comment: RA-7401. The ONLY read-only, proxy-reachable, side-effect-free backend GET that was undeclared. Found by classifying the 64 undeclared route entries against ALLOWED_UPSTREAM (dashboard/lib/pi-ceo-proxy-allowlist.ts): only 9 are proxy-reachable at all, and 7 of those spawn work (build, scan, goal-ticket, goal-projects POST, session kill/resume) so must never be smoke-probed, while the 9th needs a live session id. The other 55 undeclared entries are deliberately not proxied and therefore cannot be undeclared DASHBOARD surfaces. No body_contains: the payload is Supabase-backed data whose keys are not a fixed envelope, and asserting on data rather than contract is what makes a manifest look thorough while asserting nothing.
